title: 10 Silent Auction Tips Every Planner Should Know
summary: Silent auctions might look like a low-stakes sideshow to the main event, but decisions like item count and opening bids determine whether they raise real money.

title: The Plaza Hotel Is Closing for Four Years. Who Pays When Events Get Canceled?
summary: The Plaza won’t be the last hotel to close with events on the books. For planners booking years in advance, the closure is a reminder to review what their contracts say happens next.

title: Naboo Buys UK’s Pro-ven, Betting AI Can Make Small Meetings Profitable
summary: Naboo believes that small meetings will become worth centralizing once AI handles the admin. If that holds, procurement will gain control over a category planners and local agencies have traditionally owned.

title: Staff Shortage: Is It a Talent Gap or a Retention Problem?
summary: Meeting and event organizations can't solve retention challenges by simply hiring faster. Hiring from new talent pools, telling the real story of the work, and pairing flexibility with structure give people reasons to stay.

title: 5 Proactive Moves Meeting Planners Should Make Now
summary: BCD M&E’s latest trends report argues that 2027 events will be won or lost in the planning phase. Measurement, risk, and sustainability are all moving to the front of the process.

title: Is an Empty Storefront the New Ballroom?
summary: Vacant storefronts may seem like eyesores, but they can represent a real opportunity for planners who want blank walls and a contemporary sense of cool. The downside: They lack the built-in convenience of a traditional event environment.

title: Why a Destination’s Biggest Draws Are Also Your Best Planning Tools
summary: When evaluating destinations home to iconic attractions, meeting planners face a common dilemma: How can they leverage the destination’s mass appeal without distracting from the event’s purpose? A new white paper from Visit Anaheim answers that question — not just for planners, but the C-suite team they need to convince.

title: U.S. Ski Resorts Disappear From Canadian Trade Show, but It’s Not All About Politics
summary: American ski resorts began abandoning an Ottawa trade show before U.S.-Canada relations soured. Now, even as Canadian bookings show signs of recovery, some exhibitors have no plans to return. For organizers, the bigger challenge may be proving that trade shows are still worth the investment.

title: SPIN Aims to Reclaim Its Place in the Meetings Industry
summary: SPIN spent years as a members-only Facebook group. Now it wants a seat alongside MPI and PCMA. Can a free, volunteer-run association of veteran planners build that kind of influence?

title: Is It Time to Say "Last Call" to the Open Bar?
summary: The open bar is no longer the default icebreaker. Planners who pair quality zero-proof drinks with activities and smarter timing give every attendee a reason to stay and connect. At Skift Meetings Forum 2026, planners compared notes on shrinking bar tabs, pricey mocktails, and receptions built around more than drinks.
